C3.title: The frightening call
C3.tag: A caller turns fear into a payment
C3.brief: Meera has brought a fictional phone to the kiosk. Inspect the conversations, identify the pressure tactics, and rebuild what happened. No real money is used.
C3.closing: Case closed. You checked the evidence, named the tactics, and chose a safer response.
C3.debrief.mechanism: The sender creates a story, adds pressure, discourages outside checks, and asks for money or account access.
C3.debrief.c1: Pause before responding to a message that creates pressure.
C3.debrief.c2: Verify the claim through a contact you find independently.
C3.debrief.c3: Protect your payment details and ask a trusted person for help.
C3-CH01.explain: This detail provides context but does not by itself prove a scam. Check the request and identity, not the colour or tone.
C3-V1: This video call is from the Special Investigation Desk. Our badge proves it.
C3-01.explain: A uniform, video background or badge on a call can be fabricated. Verify through an independently found official contact.

C3-05.explain: A caller asking to move savings to an account they control is trying to take the money.

C3-06.explain: Sharing an OTP or banking screen exposes access. Keep these private regardless of the caller’s title.

C3.fix.q: What is the safest next step?
C3.fix.safe: Stop the conversation, verify independently, and ask a trusted person for help.
C3.fix.safe.why: This removes the pressure and gives you a reliable way to check the request.
C3.fix.pay: Send the money first and check later.
C3.fix.pay.why: Sending money first gives the sender what they want before the claim is verified.
C3.fix.share: Share the requested account details to settle the matter.
C3.fix.share.why: Account secrets and device access should stay private, regardless of the story.
C3.replay.1: The sender starts a story to attract attention.
C3.replay.2: A claimed identity or frightening statement makes the story feel important.
C3.replay.3: A deadline creates pressure to act.
C3.replay.5: The sender asks for money, secrets, or control of the device.
